main_body: A pew seen end-on (east/west side): a tall backrest plank on the left and a seat with a red cushion panel on the right, drawn as a side profile
top_band: none for the main body; only a 2-row light brown band (rows 14-15) at the top of the red panel and a 2-row band (rows 27-28) between the red panels, both sitting inside the front face, plus the backrest's narrow top cap (rows 9-12)
evidence: The drawing is an L-shaped side profile: a tall backrest column on the left and a lower body on the right with two red cushion panels stacked vertically. The column scan at x=8 and x=11 shows a 2-row light band (rows 14-15), then red (rows 16-25), a dark row, another 2-row band, red again, and a dark row, then the base. These are vertical faces stacked one above another, not a seat surface seen from above. No horizontal seat surface is visible, and the 2-row band is a rim at most, so it fails the 3/4 contract as a side elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 8 colours per tile against 17-20. Flat-fill coverage is 22%, higher than the stall's 13%. The red panels are large areas of one flat colour with no grain, and the wood has only about 3 steps. The outline is a tinted dark brown (2% neutral), which is acceptable, but the shading and texture are clearly thinner than the references.
